name: Austin
industries: Software and semiconductors, EV manufacturing and a maturing startup ecosystem drive an agile-leaning project market.
intro:
Austin turned itself into a first-tier tech city in a decade: Tesla's gigafactory, Apple's second-largest campus, Oracle's headquarters and a startup scene that kept its slacker-city creativity while adding enterprise scale. Delivery roles here skew agile — Scrum credentials are effectively assumed in the software economy — while the hardware and manufacturing build-out adds classical program management demand. Austin employers hire nationally and screen on credentials. Batches are scheduled live online across the whole year at hours built for Austin: a weekend Sat–Sun cohort and a weekday Wed–Thu cohort each week, all landing in comfortable local daytime; every upcoming date and its exact Austin timing is listed in the schedule below. Whatever the schedule, the format holds: one weekend, live instruction, exam application support, mocks, and trainer access until you're certified.

Austin's project culture is a merger in progress: relocated tech giants and homegrown product companies brought agile delivery expectations, while the semiconductor and infrastructure build-out around the metro runs classical capital-project governance. Professionals who certify across both traditions fit the widest set of req sheets in central Texas. The course runs live online over two consecutive days in Central time, Austin's own zone. Compensation here still carries relocation-era momentum — the sourced Austin entries in the salary table below give current, dated figures rather than boom-era anecdotes. The employer list shows the tech-semiconductor-services mix hiring certified talent, and scaling companies formalizing delivery can certify their first PMO together in a private cohort.
